scenes.text: You take a perfect photo at the beach, except for a stranger walking right behind you. [1] One tap, and they vanish, like they were never there. [2] Let's break down how magic eraser works.

title: Magic
Eraser
data.subtitle: How AI removes things from photos

scenes.text: Here's what happens after you tap. [1] You brush over the person you want gone. [2] The app creates a mask, marking exactly those pixels. [3] Those pixels are removed, leaving a hole. [4] An inpainting model looks at everything around the hole, the sand, the waves, the sky, [5] and paints in what most likely belongs there.

That last step is called inpainting, which you met in episode fifteen. [1] The model fills a missing area, so it blends in with its surroundings. [2] It studies the nearby textures and colours, [3] continues lines and patterns, like the horizon, [4] and matches the lighting and shadows.

data.definition: Filling a missing part of an image so it blends in with everything around it.

scenes.text: Many apps even find the distractions for you. [1] First, a detection model finds objects, like people, wires and bins. [2] Then a segmentation model outlines each one, pixel by pixel. [3] And the app suggests, remove these, with just one tap.

So where will you find it? [1] Phone galleries from Google, Samsung and Apple all have their own versions. [2] Design apps like Canva and Photoshop offer generative fill. [3] And online shops use it to clean up product photos.

So when does it struggle? [1] Big areas, where there's too little around to copy from. [2] Text and faces in the background, which are hard to fake well. [3] Shadows and reflections, which sometimes get left behind. [4] And whatever was hidden behind the object, which the AI has to guess.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think magic eraser reveals what was really behind the object. [2] It doesn't, because it can't see through things. It invents a believable guess, which is why edited photos should never be treated as proof.

data.myth: Magic eraser reveals what was really behind the object.
data.fact: It can't see through things. It invents a believable guess, so edited photos aren't proof.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] You brush over what you want gone. [2] The app masks those pixels. [3] Inpainting fills the hole so it blends in. [4] And remember, it invents a guess, it doesn't reveal the truth. [5] Next, we'll learn how some AI models think before they answer. Follow AI Maastaaru!
